name: Agent Pipeline: Multi Agent Document Triage
dept: Personal build, agentic AI engineering. Python, LangGraph, Claude API.
status: Built 2026-07-30, verified on a live run over 26 documents
oneline: Five agents sort a pile of documents, decide each one, and log exactly why.
line: Five agents sort a pile of documents and log exactly why.
problem: Agentic AI is easy to claim on a CV and hard to prove. Job specs ask for LangGraph and I had nothing runnable to point at.
did: I built a LangGraph state graph: four specialist agents (classifier, extractor, validator, router) under a supervisor that owns retry, escalation and degradation. Two agents call the model, two are pure Python rules.
proofNote: The proof page comes straight from the run files. All 26 documents are synthetic, so accuracy is on data of that shape.
before: Agentic AI is the easiest thing on a CV to claim and the hardest to prove. Job specs name LangGraph, CrewAI and AutoGen by name, and workflow tooling plus good prompts is not the same thing as an orchestration framework. I had no runnable multi agent build to point at.
after: A LangGraph state graph with four specialist agents (classifier, extractor, validator, router) and a supervisor that owns retry with backoff, escalation and graceful degradation. Verified on a live run against Claude over 26 synthetic property and finance documents: 26 of 26 routing decisions and 25 of 25 document types matched the ground truth manifest, across 50 model calls and 301 audit events. 267 unit tests cover the rules and the routing and never touch the network.
how: Supervisor and workers. Every worker has exactly one outgoing edge, back to the supervisor, and the supervisor owns the only conditional edge, so there is exactly one place in the system where a document's path is decided. That cycle is what makes retry, skip and escalation possible without copying retry logic into every agent.

Two agents read, two agents decide. The classifier and the extractor call the model, because reading prose is what a language model is for. The validator and the router are pure Python, because a finance manager asking why an invoice was rejected should get a rule code and a number, not a model's opinion. It also makes every routing decision unit testable with no network call.

Structured output, then checked again. Model calls are constrained by a JSON schema, and the payload is validated a second time in Python, because a schema cannot express that a confidence must sit between zero and one. A payload that fails is retried with the specific problem fed back as a correction hint.

A schema that lets the model say not stated. Every field is nullable on the wire and requiredness is enforced as a business rule, because the first revision that did it the other way round gave the model no way to report a missing due date, so it supplied one. A schema that cannot express absence converts a missing value into a fabricated one.

Routing precedence carries the safety argument. Degraded, unclassified and low confidence documents are all checked before the reject test, so the pipeline only rejects on data it actually trusts. A degraded document can never auto approve.

Auditable by default. Every dispatch, retry, escalation, rule finding and decision is a JSON line with a timestamp, document id, node and attempt number, and every tunable number lives in one policy file with a version stamped onto each decision.
value: Executable proof of multi agent orchestration in Python
risk: All 26 input documents are synthetic and every address in them is on a .example domain. No real company, person, supplier, tenant or deal anywhere in the project. Accuracy is measured against that synthetic corpus, written alongside the rules, so it shows the pipeline does what it says on data of this shape and is not a claim about real supplier invoices. Self reported model confidence is used as a triage signal with a floor, not as a probability. LangGraph and the Anthropic SDK are genuinely used; LangChain chat wrappers, CrewAI and AutoGen are not installed, not imported and not claimed.

problem: The source system keeps a status column and no history. Nobody can answer what fraction of deals reach offer, because yesterday's status was overwritten today.
did: I built a star schema warehouse on PostgreSQL: two Type 2 slowly changing dimensions so history reports as it was, 84 monthly partitions on the event fact, 51 data quality assertions, and six measured performance case studies.

how: One command starts PostgreSQL 16 in Docker, applies the schema, loads the data and runs every query with the SQL echoed.
Schema. Brokers and properties as lookup tables, deals as the fact table, with foreign keys, a unique message ID dedupe key and check constraints on status and value.

Query. Ten queries in escalating difficulty: WHERE and ORDER BY, inner joins, a LEFT JOIN with GROUP BY, HAVING, date bucketing, a NOT EXISTS subquery, and RANK with a windowed percentage share.
